reading: A full-height column sits at the left edge. Draw a 2-coloured anti-diagonal from the top-right corner down-left until it meets the column, then fill the bottom row (right of the column) with 4.

new_rows.name: antidiag
new_rows.datalog:
wmax(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
hmax(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
fgc(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
antidiag(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !fgc(Y, X), wmax(W), hmax(H), S = Y + X, S = W, Y < H.

new_rows.name: bottom_row
new_rows.datalog:
hmax(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
fgc(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
bottom_row(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !fgc(Y, X), hmax(H), Y = H.

why: background cells with Y+X = width-1 above the last row become 2; background cells of the last row become 4; nothing else changes

reading: One of the 0-coloured block shapes (the one level with a 5-coloured triangle) loses its 2-cell protrusion, and its column on the side facing that triangle turns 6. The other 0-shapes are unchanged.

slots.subject: the 0-shape that shares rows with the 5-coloured triangle
slots.removed: cells of the subject outside its main rectangle (the protrusion), set to background
slots.marked: the subject rectangle's column nearest the 5-triangle, recoloured 6

why: only the selected 0-shape changes: its protrusion becomes background and its facing edge column becomes 6

reading: Four same-coloured cells mark the corners of a box around a shape of another colour. Recolour the shape to the corner colour and cut out the box interior (excluding the corner rows and columns).

new_rows.name: inner_box
new_rows.datalog:
ymin(min(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
ymax(max(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
xmin(min(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
xmax(max(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
inner_box(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), ymin(A), ymax(B), xmin(P), xmax(Q), Y > A, Y < B, X > P, X < Q.

new_rows.name: inner_fg
new_rows.datalog:
ymin(min(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
ymax(max(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
xmin(min(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
xmax(max(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
inner_fg(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), ymin(A), ymax(B), xmin(P), xmax(Q), Y > A, Y < B, X > P, X < Q.

why: the only foreground cells on the bounding box of all foreground are the four corner markers; the output is the strict interior of that box with every shape cell in the marker colour

reading: Each isolated 3 gets a fixed 5x5 house pattern centred on it (5 roof, 2 walls, 8 floor), and the floor row is extended across the whole grid in 2.

new_rows.name: floor_row
new_rows.datalog:
fgc(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
nb(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, cell(Y2, X2, C2).
iso(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), !nb(Y, X).
floor_row(Y, X) :- iso(Y0, X0), Y = Y0 + 2, px(Y, X, C), !fgc(Y, X).

why: the row two below every marker is 2 except under the stamp, where the unit's 88888 row overwrites it; one identical unit copy centred on every marker

reading: Two vertical 5-coloured posts each capped by an 8 above and below define a rectangle; output that rectangle (posts plus caps) cut from the input.

new_rows.name: post_box
new_rows.datalog:
top(min(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C), C = 5.
bot(max(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C), C = 5.
post_box(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), C = 5.
post_box(Y, X) :- cell(Y0, X, C), C = 5, top(T), Y0 = T, Y = T - 1.
post_box(Y, X) :- cell(Y0, X, C), C = 5, bot(B), Y0 = B, Y = B + 1.

why: the output is exactly the box spanning the 5-cells extended one row up and down

reading: A thick 5-coloured band crosses the grid; every scattered single cell takes the band's colour and slides straight toward the band until it touches it (or a cell already stuck to it), stacking.

new_rows.name: dots
new_rows.datalog:
osize(O, count(Y, X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
dots(Y, X) :- obj(O, Y, X), osize(O, N), N = 1.

why: each single cell becomes 5 and ends adjacent to the band (or to a cell already attached) on its own row/column, perpendicular to the band
invariants: count of dots per row/column side

reading: Each isolated 5 gets a ring of 1 around it (3x3 square of 1 with the 5 in the centre).
why: one identical 3x3 copy centred on every marker; all other cells unchanged

reading: The grid is a lattice of 5x5 framed panels; a panel that is an empty frame receives the inner pattern of another panel of the same frame colour that has one. Panels with no same-colour patterned partner stay as they are.

slots.cells: 5x5 framed panels separated by background rows/columns
slots.source: the panel of colour c whose 3x3 interior is non-empty
slots.target: each panel of colour c whose interior is empty
slots.action: paste source interior into target interior

why: every empty-interior panel whose colour has a patterned panel ends with that pattern; all other cells unchanged

reading: Each 1-coloured cup (box with a one-cell gap in its top edge) holds one coloured seed; fill the cup interior, the gap and the row directly above the cup with the seed's colour.

new_rows.name: cup
new_rows.datalog:
osize(O, count(Y, X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
big(O) :- osize(O, N), N > 1.
inbig(Y, X) :- big(O), obj(O, Y, X).
oy0(O, min(Y)) :- big(O), obj(O, Y, X).
oy1(O, max(Y)) :- big(O), obj(O, Y, X).
ox0(O, min(X)) :- big(O), obj(O, Y, X).
ox1(O, max(X)) :- big(O), obj(O, Y, X).
cup(Y, X) :- big(O), oy0(O, A), oy1(O, B), ox0(O, P), ox1(O, Q), T = A - 2, U = B + 1, R = P - 1, S = Q + 1, px(Y, X, C), Y > T, Y < U, X > R, X < S, !inbig(Y, X).

why: for each cup, every non-cup cell in its box extended one row upward takes the colour of the seed inside it

reading: Dashed 1-coloured lines form a rectangle (sometimes with an inner divider line); fill the gaps of every row or column that is a line, within the bounding box, with 2.

new_rows.name: gaps
new_rows.datalog:
fgc(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
rcount(Y, count(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
ccount(X, count(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
y0(min(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
y1(max(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
x0(min(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
x1(max(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
inbox(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), y0(A), y1(B), x0(P), x1(Q), A1 = A - 1, B1 = B + 1, P1 = P - 1, Q1 = Q + 1, Y > A1, Y < B1, X > P1, X < Q1.
gaps(Y, X) :- inbox(Y, X), !fgc(Y, X), rcount(Y, N), N > 3.
gaps(Y, X) :- inbox(Y, X), !fgc(Y, X), ccount(X, N), N > 3.

why: background cells inside the foreground bounding box on a row or column holding more than 3 foreground cells become 2; nothing else changes
